message.reasoning_content:
Let me analyze this situation carefully.

The user has a position on Moonwell Base Core: cbETH supplied as collateral, USDC borrowed against it, health factor ~1.6.

Timeline:
- O01 (Feb 10): Governance proposal MIP-X43 to activate OEV wrappers for non-composite markets including cbETH on Base Core. This changes the oracle feed via setFeed() on ChainlinkOracle.
- O02 (Feb 14): Proposal passed, executable after timelock ~2026-02-15T18:00Z.
- O03 (Feb 15 17:00): Normal state — cbETH oracle $2,250.65 matching Chainlink composite. Healthy utilization.
- O04 (Feb 15 18:04:33): Governance tx changed 14 oracle feeds. Moonwell oracle price for cbETH: $2,206.68 -> $1.1227 (-99.95%). Chainlink composite still $2,206.68. So the newly activated OEV wrapper is reporting a wildly wrong price — essentially the OEV wrapper appears misconfigured or being exploited via OEV (Oracle Extractable Value). The oracle price crashed to $1.12 while the real Chainlink composite price is $2,206.68.
- O05 (Feb 15 18:04:35): 3 liquidations already occurring with cbETH collateral, seizing cbETH at the fake $1.12 oracle price. Liquidators are seizing collateral at massively discounted prices.

This is an active oracle incident: the OEV wrapper activation has caused the cbETH oracle price to report ~$1.12 instead of ~$2,206. This is causing wrongful liquidations — users' cbETH collateral is being seized at 0.05% of its real value.

The user's position: cbETH collateral, USDC borrowed, HF ~1.6. With the oracle reporting cbETH at $1.12 instead of $2,206, the user's collateral value as seen by the protocol has collapsed by 99.95%. Their health factor as computed by the protocol is now effectively near zero (collateral value ~0.05% of before). They will be liquidated immediately — in fact liquidations are already happening (O05).

Wait — but the liquidations seize cbETH collateral. The user's position would be liquidated: their cbETH collateral seized to repay USDC debt. At the fake oracle price, the liquidator seizes collateral worth (real terms) far more than the debt repaid. This is a catastrophic loss for the user — they'd lose essentially all their cbETH for a small USDC debt.

What can the user do? They cannot move funds directly; they propose an action; corridor limits enforce safety. Actions: hold, reduce_light, reduce_to_target, exit, relever.

In this situation:
- The oracle is broken (reporting $1.12). Any attempt to interact with the protocol... Hmm. If the user tries to repay debt and withdraw, would the protocol allow it? Withdrawing collateral: the protocol checks borrow balance vs collateral at the fake oracle price. Actually with the oracle at $1.12, the user's collateral is valued at nearly zero, so they're undercollateralized per the protocol. Can they still repay USDC and withdraw cbETH? Repaying debt reduces borrow; withdrawing collateral... typically you can withdraw if it doesn't leave the position undercollateralized. If collateral is valued at ~zero, any withdrawal leaves them undercollateralized... Actually if they repay ALL debt first, then they can withdraw all collateral. Repaying all USDC debt requires having USDC. The keeper "cannot move funds, only propose an action" — hmm, the keeper proposes actions like exit which presumably executes repay + withdraw.

But wait — there's a race: liquidations are already happening. The user's position with HF 1.6 at real prices is now, at fake prices, massively undercollateralized (collateral valued at 0.05% of real). Liquidators can seize the entire collateral. Actually with the oracle at $1.12, liquidators repay USDC debt and seize cbETH at the fake price — they seize up to (closeFactor) collateral per liquidation, and can repeat. The user's position will be fully liquidated within seconds/minutes.

The best action: exit — repay USDC debt and withdraw cbETH immediately, racing the liquidations. Even if there's a chance some ops fail, exit is the only action that attempts to save the position. Alternatively, is there any argument the position is safe? No — liquidations are confirmed happening on cbETH collateral at the broken oracle price.

Risk level: critical. Action: exit.

Could there be an argument for reduce_to_target? No — the position is being liquidated right now at a 99.95% mispriced oracle. Partial reduction doesn't help; the whole collateral is at risk of being seized at fake prices. Exit now.

One consideration: can the user even withdraw? If the oracle price is broken low, the user's borrow (USDC) is fine, collateral valued near zero. To exit: repay USDC debt (needs USDC — the keeper presumably has or the position structure allows flash repay? Not our concern; we propose exit). Then withdraw cbETH. If they can't repay fully, partial. Either way, exit is the right proposal. Also note: liquidations seize collateral only up to the debt repaid; if the user repays their own debt first, no more liquidation incentive.

Also note the possibility that this is an OEV wrapper exploit — MEV extraction via oracle updates (OEV = Oracle Extractable Value). The wrapper may have been exploited or misconfigured such that an OEV searcher pushed a malicious price. Either way, the protocol's oracle for cbETH is reporting $1.12 and liquidations are executing against it. This is an active, ongoing loss event for cbETH suppliers/borrowers on Moonwell Base.

Risk: critical. Action: exit.

- Governance-activated OEV wrapper (MIP-X43, executed at timelock expiry) changed cbETH oracle feed; oracle now reports $1.12 vs Chainlink composite $2,206.68 (-99.95%).
- Liquidations against cbETH collateral are already executing at the broken price (3 liquidations, 250 cbETH seized), so the user's cbETH collateral will be seized imminently.
- User's HF 1.6 at real prices is irrelevant; protocol now values collateral at ~0.05%, making the position instantly liquidatable; full unwind (repay USDC, withdraw cbETH) before further liquidation is the only loss-avoiding action.
- Not a market move; real price unchanged — this is an oracle fault from the just-activated wrapper, so waiting for "recovery" risks total collateral loss.
